cubes.text: Your hand connects with her backside, the sound almost routine by now. She remains still, but this time the silence isn’t empty. You hear it — a soft, shaky exhale that tips into a quiet moan, barely louder than a heartbeat. It’s gone before you can trap it in your ears, leaving you paralyzed, half-convinced you imagined it.

Heart racing, you shove the plates next to the sink, too flustered to stack them. As you retreat, you risk a sideways glance, expecting the usual blank mask. Instead, you’re met with a smile — not timid, not hidden, but a slow, satisfied curve that creeps from the corner of her mouth all the way to her eyes. She doesn’t say a word, but that smile speaks volumes.
